defects.summary: Windows 10 RTM product names ("Windows 10 for x64-based Systems") derive no release and no file-index key, so every KB of that product resolves to "No file-index key is known"; the Winbindex key 1507 is unreachable.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/kbcorrelation/alias_catalog.py:27-30 (RELEASE_PATTERNS need a version token); src/patchtrace/kbcorrelation/products.py:108-130; strict xfail tests/test_kbc_audit_20261107.py:160-163
defects.failure_scenario: Checked with products.derive(): "Windows 10 for x64-based Systems" -> release None, winbindex_key None. The same holds for "Windows 10 Version 2004 for x64-based Systems" (pattern `version (1[5-9][0-9]{2})` cannot match 2004) and "Windows 11 for x64-based Systems" (the pre-rename 21H2 name; real-data occurrence of these two names is UNVERIFIED in the repo, the derivation result is verified). `kb pairs` then prints NO_KEY for a product Winbindex does cover.
defects.proposed_fix: Spec first (31-C: scope identity vs. Winbindex key; record the implied releases). alias_catalog: bump ALIAS_CATALOG_VERSION to 2; widen the numeric token to `\bversion (1[5-9][0-9]{2}|2004)\b`; add data IMPLIED_CLIENT_RELEASE = (("10", "1507"), ("11", "21H2")) and IMPLIED_NAME_PATTERN = r"^windows (10|11) for (?:x64-based|32-bit|arm64-based) systems$" (exact RTM form only, so LTSC/IoT/other names stay unkeyed). products.derive: when family is windows-client, no release token matched and the whole normalised name matches IMPLIED_NAME_PATTERN, set release from the table; the key follows as 10-1507 / 11-21H2 (resolver.index_keys already tries 1507). Scope ids of only these names change (v1 name-keyed -> v2 keyed); stored investigations on them hit the existing "mapping is no longer current; repeat the search" path.
defects.regression_test: Remove the xfail of test_kba08_windows_10_rtm_product_name_gets_a_file_index_key; add to tests/test_kbc_products.py: RTM x64 -> key "10-1507", "Version 2004" -> "10-2004", Windows 11 RTM -> "11-21H2", "Windows 10 Version 1607" scope id unchanged, an LTSC name still unkeyed, ALIAS_CATALOG_VERSION == 2; one resolver test that a "1507" record row resolves for the RTM scope.

defects.summary: lineage.predecessor() can return a row carrying the target's own bytes when the build reverted across a different-class row, so the resolver proposes a byte-identical grade X pair and hides the usable earlier build.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/kbcorrelation/lineage.py:186-207 (the backward loop never compares row.sha256 with target.sha256); strict xfail tests/test_kbc_audit_20261107.py:131-148
defects.failure_scenario: Timeline Z(std), A(std), B(preview), A(std, target KB): on main predecessor returns the first A row; resolve() answers changed_in_kb="yes" together with one pair graded X / IDENTICAL_CONTENT ("this file did not change between them") and never offers Z -> A. Simulated in memory here: main gives older=KB5000001 (same SHA); the fix gives older=KB5000000 with window (KB5000001, KB5000002), grade A + WINDOW_CONFOUNDED.
defects.proposed_fix: Decision: skip identical bytes (audit option 1). In the loop add `if row.sha256 == target.sha256: continue` before the same-class test; the skipped rows stay in the returned window so the pair is named WINDOW_CONFOUNDED. With no other row the answer is (None, ()) -> NO_OLDER. Option 2 (walk to before the earliest identical row) is wrong for Z, A, Y(std), B(preview), A: it would skip the nearest distinct standard build Y. Update the docstring and docs/specs/kb-cve/31-C-product-build-pairs.md (rule "the older side never has the target SHA"); optionally say in the NO_OLDER note when only a different-class build precedes.
defects.regression_test: Remove the xfail marker of test_kba06_predecessor_never_returns_a_row_with_the_targets_own_sha (it passes with the one-line fix; verified by in-memory simulation); add tests/test_kbc_lineage.py cases Z,A,B(preview),A -> Z and Z,A,Y,B(preview),A -> Y, and a resolver test that no returned pair carries IDENTICAL_CONTENT.

defects.summary: A pair downloaded with `kb acquire` is stored as a manual pair: its index lineage (target KB, window, grade A, fix boundary, Winbindex record hash) and the download provenance (URL, retrieval time) are not persisted anywhere, and the stored analyst decision says the analyst chose the order.
defects.evidence: src/patchtrace/kbcorrelation/acquire.py:8-10 ("it is not written into the project"), src/patchtrace/kbcorrelation/service.py:623-626 (acquire -> import_pair), src/patchtrace/kbcorrelation/service.py:678 (propose_manual), src/patchtrace/kbcorrelation/service.py:754-756 (decision text), src/patchtrace/kbcorrelation/service.py:636-638 (provenance only in the returned Outcome); no append_attempt call exists for acquire (grep: only recovery.py:37 and store.py:621)
defects.failure_scenario: Analyst acquires the grade A index-adjacent pair for KB5099001; the project context and workspace record tier E, grade B, lineage user-asserted, ORDER_UNVERIFIED and "Older and newer were chosen by the analyst; the release order was not established". `kb explain` / `kb export` a week later cannot show which KB the pair brackets, that other updates ship in the window, or where the bytes came from; that evidence existed only in one stdout document.
defects.proposed_fix: Keep the project untouched (revision rule) and persist in the workspace: pass the resolved index PairProposal and the download records into import_pair (new keyword `origin`), append an AnalystDecision op="pair-origin" whose reason names the index pair id, target KB, window KBs, reason codes and record SHA-256, word the orientation decision from the index when the pair came from it, and append Attempt(op="acquire", plan_sha, stage="imported"). Carry the index pair summary in the kb sidecar / ContextBundle only after a spec amendment (31-D, 31-F).

actionable_now.title: KB dock: read the open project through an owner-thread snapshot (KBB-01)
actionable_now.why: D-DEF-01: the dock's production loader fails with "the project cannot be opened" for every project the desktop holds; reproduced on main with the sample project.
actionable_now.risk: Project store is owner-thread only (store-threading-spec R1): every read must stay on the GUI thread; keep the CLI path (RealEngine.read by directory) unchanged.
actionable_now.acceptance: New test holds ProjectService.sample open and drives KbController with the default loader: state is ready or no-advisory, never failed; no second ProjectService.open happens (assert by monkeypatch).

actionable_now.title: KBA-06: predecessor() never returns the target's own bytes
actionable_now.why: A reverted build yields a byte-identical grade X pair and hides the usable earlier build; strict xfail exists.
actionable_now.risk: Changes which older build is proposed for reverted timelines only; pair ids of other timelines are unchanged. Spec sentence first (AGENTS.md).
actionable_now.acceptance: xfail marker removed and the test passes; Z,A,B(preview),A -> Z with window (A,B); Z,A,Y,B(preview),A -> Y; no resolver pair carries IDENTICAL_CONTENT.

actionable_now.title: KBA-08: file-index keys for Windows 10 RTM, Version 2004 and Windows 11 RTM names (alias catalog v2)
actionable_now.why: Products Winbindex covers resolve to "No file-index key is known"; strict xfail exists.
actionable_now.risk: Bumps ALIAS_CATALOG_VERSION (parse key) and changes scope ids of exactly these names; stored investigations on them must repeat the search (existing guarded path). Real MSRC use of the 2004 and Windows 11 RTM names is UNVERIFIED offline.
actionable_now.acceptance: xfail marker removed; derive() gives 10-1507, 10-2004, 11-21H2; ids of already keyed names are byte-identical to main; an LTSC name stays unkeyed.

actionable_now.title: KBA-07: report/2 accepts every canonical KB id (KB + 4-10 digits)
actionable_now.why: Latent export refusal once KB advisories are exported; strict xfail exists; prerequisite of D-T12.
actionable_now.risk: Widens an exported contract: the spec must change first; check the schema drift test.
actionable_now.acceptance: xfail marker removed; KB1234 and KB1234567890 accepted; KB123, 11 digits, lower case and non-ASCII digits rejected.

actionable_now.title: Persist index lineage and download provenance of an acquired pair
actionable_now.why: D-DEF-02: after kb acquire the stored record says the analyst chose the order and keeps no KB, window, record hash, URL or retrieval time.
actionable_now.risk: Must not advance the project revision (attach link records it): write to the workspace decisions/attempts only; AnalystDecision.reason is capped at 500 characters.
actionable_now.acceptance: After a consented fake-transport acquire, ws.decisions() has a pair-origin record naming the index pair id, target KB, window and record SHA-256, and ws.attempts() an acquire attempt with the plan_sha; the manual import path is unchanged.

actionable_now.title: kb attach: attach an investigation context to an existing analysed project
actionable_now.why: Today only projects created by kb import-pair/acquire can hold KB context (PT-KBC-UNSUPPORTED), so the chain cannot be applied to work an analyst already has, and kb leads needs a re-created, re-analysed project.
actionable_now.risk: Cross-project linkage must be refused when the project bytes differ from the pair (31-H "cross-project file link refusal"); writes one enrichment row, so the project store lock and revision rules apply.
actionable_now.acceptance: kb attach SAMPLE --investigation INV builds the pair from the project's stored artifacts, records the decisions, writes kb-context and returns attached; a second run is idempotent; kb leads then groups read_item under the CVE; a project whose SHA-256 pair differs is refused.

actionable_now.title: kb index sync: reachable --help and listed in kb index --help
actionable_now.why: D-DEF-03: the only consented CVRF fetch verb is undiscoverable and its --help errors.
actionable_now.risk: Help only; cli_index must stay import-clean of network modules.
actionable_now.acceptance: kb index sync --help exits 0 and names --consent-hosts/--consent-plan; kb index --help mentions sync.

actionable_now.title: kb leads: correct state text without a run and chip text without a context
actionable_now.why: D-DEF-04: output claims a ranking mismatch when nothing was ranked, and refers to a context that is not attached.
actionable_now.risk: The synergy golden pins lead shape; update it only if the changed strings are part of the golden.
actionable_now.acceptance: No-run note renders the no-comparison sentence plus the note; no-advisory rows say no advisory context is attached; banned-word sweep stays clean.

actionable_now.title: KEV into pilot leads and kb search edges
actionable_now.why: pilot leads always prints "CISA KEV: unknown" and kb search edges always "not-loaded" although the catalog store, CatalogKev and the kb KEV adapter exist.
actionable_now.risk: kev_snapshot_id is part of the pilot result_id: stored results become stale when a catalog is loaded (intended, must be stated). tests/conftest.py already redirects the default KEV folder; keep KEV a CVE-level fact that never orders functions.
actionable_now.acceptance: With a synthetic catalog (tests/fixtures/kbcorrelation/kev-synthetic.json imported into a temp KEV dir) pilot leads shows listed + date for the listed CVE and "not in snapshot" otherwise; kb search --json edges carry the same states; without a catalog both stay unknown / not-loaded.

actionable_now.title: CLI verb to run the comparison of one two-file project
actionable_now.why: The CLI chain stops after kb import-pair: only series create --run (3-8 builds) or the desktop start Ghidriff.
actionable_now.risk: cli.py is a shared integrator file and backend.py belongs to L2/L5: reuse the existing _run_pair / run_comparison call unchanged and add no backend code. Verifiable here only with the hermetic fake Ghidriff used by the series tests; live behaviour stays unverified.
actionable_now.acceptance: patchtrace compare PROJECT --python P --ghidra-dir G (fake backend) records a completed run, is a no-op on a project that already has one, exits 5 on cancel, and rank + kb leads then work on the same project.

actionable_now.title: kb identify: binary-first lookup of a local file in saved Winbindex records
actionable_now.why: Hops 2-4 start from the binary in the target chain, but nothing maps a file to its build, KB and product; the analyst must already know the KB.
actionable_now.risk: Index rows are claims: the answer must be labelled index claim, list every version key the SHA appears under, and say "not in the saved record" instead of guessing from the version resource. New contract surface: spec first.
actionable_now.acceptance: For a record whose row SHA equals the synthetic PE, kb identify FILE prints version key, KB (or BASE), UBR, heading class, the next and previous distinct builds and the CVEs the index lists for that KB; an unknown SHA exits 4 with the stated gap.

actionable_now.title: report/2: export the KB context as kind=kb and kind=cve advisories
actionable_now.why: The consolidated report omits the KB chain; kb export is a separate file.
actionable_now.risk: Export must not write to the project (adapters.py guards this for pilot); advisory text is untrusted and goes through the existing inert-text path.
actionable_now.acceptance: A kb-created project exports one kb record per KB of the lead and one cve record per card with the source snapshot digest; a project without a context is unchanged byte for byte.

actionable_now.title: L1 join runner over the candidate manifest (offline, synthetic test)
actionable_now.why: The 87-case L1 corpus has never been run through the join; no runner exists.
actionable_now.risk: Never score a case marked facts: unverified (AGENTS.md); the runner must report per-layer L1 only and refuse an unfrozen manifest for a scored run. Real months are unavailable here, so only the mechanics are verified.
actionable_now.acceptance: Against a synthetic manifest and the synthetic month the runner reports per case: KB edge found, product scope found, expected file resolvable, with counts; unverified cases are listed and excluded.

actionable_now.title: kb products --all / --query: stored-product catalogue from the CLI
actionable_now.why: GUI-only capability (browse_products and the product-only start); KbService.product_catalogue is already built.
actionable_now.risk: Argument shape of an existing verb changes (INV becomes optional with --all): keep the old form working.
actionable_now.acceptance: kb products --all --query 24H2 lists the stored scopes with exit 0 and exit 4 when none match; no investigation is created.

A byte-identical pair says "this file did not change between them"; every context, lead, report and export carries the limitation that it does not show a function contains or fixes a CVE; the pilot gate "applies" comes from CSAF product status, and the mechanism tier "strong" is unreachable. summary: Offline, an analyst can run the KB chain by CLI from advisory import to an attached, exportable context; I ran it on synthetic fixtures. It stops at comparison: no Ghidra here, and no single-pair CLI verb. `pilot leads/why/review` and `kb leads` work on the sample project. Nothing claims a fix because binaries differ. No recommendation record exists, only lead classes and next-step sentences. One high defect: the KB dock cannot load the open project (reproduced). Medium: KBA-06, KBA-08 (plus two sibling names), acquired-pair provenance not persisted. KBA-06..08 have fix designs; the KBA-06 fix was simulated and flips its xfail. Evidence is synthetic or mocked throughout; none is live.
